label: v5 design phase (4 m windows), foresight
step_form_formula: E = cost(mean map); sd = sum over contact nodes n of |c_eff[n]| * sqrt(C[u(n), u(n)]), u(n) = u_idx[n, argmax_j means[n, j]] the mean-map winner cell of node n; no max, no covariance (per-step Gaussian-CVaR proxy)

arm_NLL_spread.note: max-min mean NLL across the variance arms, before and after the recalibration; the factor is how much of the scale a ranking is read on the k-rescale destroys

mean-map.note: point prediction, no predicted variance: mean_NLL / cov1 / cov2 / sd_ratio / mean_z do not exist for this arm and are null by construction, not omitted

belief_referee.referee: belief MC, raw Var, no truth, no recalibration

sd_deficit_vs_alpha.note: REPORTED CHARACTERIZATION, no criterion. clark's belief-referee sd-ratio (sd_clark / sd_MC) binned by the window's cost-weighted median alpha. The historical record is 0.90-0.94; the derived worst case is ~0.89 at alpha ~ 0.

cvar_error.note: REPORTED CHARACTERIZATION, no criterion. |CVaR_q(arm) - CVaR_q(MC)| per window under the belief referee -- the single number a planner consumes, fusing both moments through the decision rule's own tail weight. The arm CVaR is the Gaussian form E + phi(z_q)/(1-q) * sd; the MC CVaR is the mean of the empirical upper tail. mean-map has no sd, so its CVaR is its point prediction -- the floor a risk-blind planner sits at.
